newsitem.title: USA: Junk US corporates close mixed, high-grades stable.
newsitem.headline: Junk US corporates close mixed, high-grades stable.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds ended mixed on Thursday on a day of active trading, while spreads in the investment-grade corporate bond market were largely unchanged amid sluggish volume, traders said.

New issue activity in the junk market continued at a brisk pace with CANTV, a Venezuelan telephone company, selling $200 million in five- and seven-year notes via Chase Securities Inc and Atlantic Express Transportation Corp selling $110 milion in senior secured notes via Jeffries & Co Inc.
Late in the day, Vintage Petroleum Inc sold $100 million in senior subordinated notes due 2009 via Salomon Brothers Inc.

In the junk sector, traders offered various views on the performance of the market, with some arguing that bond prices increased 1/8 of a point on average, and others maintaining that bonds dropped 1/4 to 1/2 of a point on average.
All traders, however, agreed that the paper sector was particularly weak on Thursday.

"I think people's initial enthusiasm that the paper cycle would turn up quickly is giving way to a view that the upturn is at least six to nine-months away," said Paul Greenberg, head of high-yield research at Bear Stearns & Co Inc and paper sector analyst.
Greenberg believes there is further risk that junk bonds in the sector will weaken if paper price increases do not materialize.
Stone Container 10.75 percent first mortgage notes dropped to 102 3/4 from 104 1/2 on speculation that the company would have weak upcoming earnings, a trader said.
Traders said Riverwood International 10.875 percent subordinated notes dropped almost two points as word spread that an investor had sold a large chunk of the company's bank debt.
The bonds later shaved one point off their losses when word spread that the bank loan position was not as large as investors had initially suspected, a trader said.
Elsewhere, Penn Traffic Co bonds dropped to 30-30 1/2 from 35-35 1/2 on continued negative sentiment about the supermarket company's outlook, traders said.

In the secondary market for investment-grade bonds, TCI Communications Inc debt tightened 10 basis points as investors weighed the impact of the National Association of Insurance Commissioner's move to downgrade the company's rating.
The NAIC's action caused the bonds to widen 20 basis points late on Wednesday.
New issuance of investment-grade bonds tapered off on Thursday following the previous day's flood of new supply.
Houston Lighting and Power was one of several issuers to sell trust preferred stock on Thursday. The utility sold $100 million of the securities via Goldman Sachs & Co.

In the government market, Treasuries ended higher for the third straight session as the market expressed relief that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan did not focus on the economy in Congressional testimony.
The 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 15/32 to 95-10/32 yielding 6.87 percent.
